Accept a resume, store it, and queue it for processing.

Returns as soon as the artifact is durable and a processing run exists. The
pipeline — extraction, OCR, a model call — happens on a worker, so how long
a resume takes to read has no bearing on how long this request takes to
answer.

Returns 201 for a new document and 200 when these exact bytes were already
uploaded by this user, which makes a retried request idempotent rather than
duplicating the resume.

get.description: The structured reading, for the review screen.

post.description:
Try again. Always a new run, never a reopened one.

Refused with a 409 when the previous attempt is still in flight, or when it
failed for a reason the same bytes will reproduce.

Ingest a job posting.

Returns 201 for a new job — structured and ready to review in the same
response — and 200 when this exact identity already existed, unchanged.
Idempotent for the same reason resume upload is: a client retrying after a
timeout must not create a second copy of what it already submitted.

schema.title: Response List Jobs Api V1 Jobs Get

get.description:
The structured reading, for the review screen.

`requirements` is null until a run has completed — a job just ingested and
still processing, or one whose only attempt failed, has a `run` to show
and nothing structured yet. Never an error: absence of a result is not the
same fact as failure to produce one, and the run itself already says which
is true.

post.description:
Try structuring again. Always a new run, never a reopened one — the
same discipline resume reprocessing uses, for the same reason: rewriting a
finished attempt would destroy the record of what it actually produced.

Match a confirmed profile version against this job's requirements.

201 when the evaluation is new, 200 when this exact evaluation already
existed — idempotent for the same reason job ingestion is: a client
retrying after a timeout must not create a second copy of the same
judgment.

409 when the job has not been structured yet, or when the named version is
a draft: both are states where a match would be meaningless rather than
merely empty.

get.description: This caller's matches for this job, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Matches Api V1 Jobs  Job Id  Matches Get

get.description: One match in full, with every requirement verdict and its evidence.

post.description:
Generate a resume for this job from a confirmed profile version.

Returns as soon as the run is durable. Generation, grounding validation and
rendering happen on a worker, so how long a model takes has no bearing on
how long this request takes to answer.

201 when a run was opened, 200 when one for the same job and version is
already in flight — which makes a double-click resolve to the run that is
already going rather than racing a second one against it.

409 when the job has not been structured yet, or when the named version is a
draft: both are states where a tailored resume would be meaningless rather
than merely empty.

get.description: This caller's tailored resumes for this job, newest first.

get.description: Every tailored resume this caller owns, newest first.

schema.title: Response List All Api V1 Tailored Resumes Get

get.description: One run in full: the document, every grounding finding, the artifact.

The generated file.

Everything that decides whether this is allowed lives in
`service.get_artifact` — ownership, completion, the grounding verdict and
whether the object is actually in storage. This handler's only job is to
attach the filename and the content type the artifact row recorded.

`Content-Disposition` carries a filename built server-side from the job and
the profile version, sanitised at the point it is generated
(`rendering.build_filename`). It is never echoed from client input.

Resume processing that needs operational attention.

By default: exhausted retry budgets, permanent failures, and runs nobody is
working on. Healthy documents are left out — a view that listed everything
would bury the handful that matter, which is the failure mode of most
operational dashboards.

`counts` covers every state regardless of the filter, so one glance
distinguishes a single bad document from an outage.

parameters.description: Return every document's state, not only the ones needing attention.

get.description:
Every attempt made on one document.

Not scoped to an owner: an operator investigating a failure has been given a
document id by someone, and refusing it because it belongs to a different
user would make the endpoint useless for its only purpose.

One attempt, with its stage timings.

Event `detail` is projected to `code` and `classification`. The column is
unconstrained JSONB documented as counts and codes only — true of every
writer today and enforced by nothing, which is not a guarantee worth
extending across users.

ArtifactRead.title: ArtifactRead
ArtifactRead.description: What the user is told about the file. Never where it lives.

AttentionList.title: AttentionList
AttentionList.description: The answer to "show me what needs operational attention".

CandidateContact.title: CandidateContact
CandidateContact.description:
Who the resume says this is and how to reach them.

Separate from the career sections because it is the one part of a resume
that is not an event in a history — it has no dates and cannot repeat.

value.title: Value
value.description: Normalized date, or null when the text cannot be normalized

precision.title: Precision
precision.description: How precisely the resume stated it. 'May 2024' is 'month'.

CandidateDate.title: CandidateDate
CandidateDate.description: A date as the resume expressed it, plus a normalization we can justify.

CandidateLink.title: CandidateLink
CandidateLink.description:
A URL the resume carries, and the words it was written as.

The label is what the document showed ("Github"); the url is where it
pointed. Both are kept because a resume that renders every link as the word
"GitHub" gives the reader nothing to tell two repositories apart.

CandidateSummary.title: CandidateSummary
CandidateSummary.description:
The resume's own summary or objective paragraph, as written.

Never composed by us from the rest of the document: a summary the candidate
did not write is a claim they did not make.

ContactItem.title: ContactItem
ContactItem.description:
How to reach the person this profile describes.

Every field is optional: a resume that gives a name and nothing else is a
resume, and refusing it would fail the whole snapshot over a missing phone
number.

DocumentProcessingDetail.title: DocumentProcessingDetail
DocumentProcessingDetail.description:
One document, and every attempt made on it.

The full history rather than the latest attempt, because the history is the
diagnosis: three attempts failing on the same provider code is a different
problem from three failing on different ones.

DocumentProcessingSummary.title: DocumentProcessingSummary
DocumentProcessingSummary.description:
One document's processing state.

Carries `user_id` and not the user's email: an operator needs to correlate a
support request, and a listing of every candidate's address is a mailing
list. Resolving an id to a person is a separate, separately authorised step
that does not exist yet.

JobCandidate.title: JobCandidate
JobCandidate.description: The structured reading of one job's description.

JobDetail.title: JobDetail
JobDetail.description:
A single job in full — including the description as normalized, which
is the closest thing to "raw" this API exposes: the posting's own text,
untouched by any structurer.

JobIngestionRequest.title: JobIngestionRequest
JobIngestionRequest.description:
A job posting as an extension would submit it.

Every field here is validated at the edge — type, length, URL scheme — but
nothing is yet NORMALIZED: `employment_type` arrives as whatever text the
source site used ("Full-time", "FULL_TIME", "Contract - W2"), not yet
mapped to the closed vocabulary `Job.employment_type` enforces. That
mapping is `app/services/job/normalization.py`'s job, deliberately kept
separate from validation — validation decides whether a payload is
well-formed at all; normalization decides what a well-formed field means.

is_terminal.title: Is Terminal
is_terminal.description: Whether this attempt has stopped. Everything else is in progress.

can_retry.title: Can Retry
can_retry.description:
Whether offering the user a retry button would be honest.

False for a failure the same job text and configuration will
reproduce — an AI provider's content refusal does not change on the
second attempt, and a button that says otherwise is a lie.

JobProcessingRunRead.title: JobProcessingRunRead
JobProcessingRunRead.description:
One processing attempt, as the owning user sees it.

Exposing `error_message` here is safe in a way it would not be on a
surface reading across users: this is the same person who submitted the
job, asking about their own run.

source_section.title: Source Section
source_section.description: The heading this claim was found under, if one was identified.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Text copied verbatim from the description. Never paraphrased.

JobProvenance.title: JobProvenance
JobProvenance.description:
Where a requirement came from, and how sure the structurer was.

`source_section` is the mirror of resume's `page`: a job description has no
pages, but it usually has headings ("Requirements", "Nice to have",
"Responsibilities"), and naming the one a claim came from is what makes the
claim checkable by a person reading the original posting.

JobQualificationItem.title: JobQualificationItem
JobQualificationItem.description:
The catch-all: claims that are real requirements but do not fit skills,
experience, education, certifications or technologies — work authorization,
travel expectations, on-call rotations, security clearance, and where the
job is ("Based in Berlin", "Remote within Germany").

Location statements live here deliberately rather than in a list of their
own. `engine.evaluate` iterates a fixed set of JobCandidate lists, so a new
`locations` list it did not read would make those requirements vanish from
a match result entirely — shrinking the denominator, which is the one way a
coverage score can mislead without any individual verdict being wrong. A
structured location item belongs with the engine branch that reads it, not
ahead of it.

JobRequirementsRead.title: JobRequirementsRead
JobRequirementsRead.description: The structured reading of one job, for the review screen.

JobRequirementsResponse.title: JobRequirementsResponse
JobRequirementsResponse.description:
Everything the review screen needs about one job's newest reading.

`requirements` is the newest reading that exists — the one matching and
tailoring use — and `run` is the attempt that produced it. After a failed
reprocess that is an EARLIER attempt than `job.latest_run`, which still
reports the failure: `run.id != job.latest_run.id` is the signal. When no
attempt has produced a reading yet, `requirements` is null and `run` is
the latest attempt, so a job still processing, or whose every attempt
failed, still shows its state.

JobResponsibilityItem.title: JobResponsibilityItem
JobResponsibilityItem.description:
Responsibilities describe the role, not a bar to clear — there is no
required/preferred axis for what a job asks someone to do once hired.

JobSummary.title: JobSummary
JobSummary.description:
A job as it appears in a listing — enough to recognize it and its
processing state, not the full description.

has_unmet_required.title: Has Unmet Required
has_unmet_required.description:
Whether any required requirement is unmet or unsettled.

Derived on the server so a client cannot invent its own rule, and
deliberately phrased as "unmet" rather than as a suitability verdict:
§13 forbids this engine from concluding a candidate is unsuitable. It
says what the counts say, nothing more.

MatchDetail.title: MatchDetail
MatchDetail.description: A match in full: every requirement verdict, with its evidence.

MatchEvidenceRead.title: MatchEvidenceRead
MatchEvidenceRead.description:
A profile-version row that justifies — or fails to justify — a verdict.

`qualifies` is the field that makes an UNCERTAIN explainable. Evidence
that fell short is returned rather than dropped, with `note` saying why,
so a user reading a gap sees what the matcher found and what it wanted
instead of an empty list.

profile_version_id.title: Profile Version Id
profile_version_id.description: The confirmed profile version to match. Defaults to the caller's current confirmed version. Drafts are refused.

MatchRequest.title: MatchRequest
MatchRequest.description: What a caller may ask for when creating a match.

MatchSummary.title: MatchSummary
MatchSummary.description: A match as it appears in a listing: the counts, not the verdicts.

ProcessingResultRead.title: ProcessingResultRead
ProcessingResultRead.description: Everything the review screen needs about one run.

ProcessingRunDetail.title: ProcessingRunDetail
ProcessingRunDetail.description: One run, with its stage timings.

is_terminal.title: Is Terminal
is_terminal.description: Whether this attempt has stopped. Everything else is in progress.

is_waiting_to_retry.title: Is Waiting To Retry
is_waiting_to_retry.description:
Whether this attempt exists but is deliberately not started yet.

The difference between "a worker is reading your resume" and "we are
waiting before trying again", which are the same `status` and would
otherwise be the same thing on screen.

can_retry.title: Can Retry
can_retry.description:
Whether offering the user a retry button would be honest.

False while a run is in flight, and false for a failure the same bytes
will reproduce — a corrupt file does not become readable on the second
attempt, and a button that says otherwise is a lie. True for a failure
the deployment caused (no OCR engine, a revoked key): hiding the button
there left the document with no way forward once the deployment was
fixed. Mirrors `retry.manual_retry_refusal`, from the same rule.

ProcessingRunRead.title: ProcessingRunRead
ProcessingRunRead.description:
One processing attempt, as the UI sees it.

Deliberately absent: the lease. Who holds a run and until when is an
operational fact, and exposing it would invite a client to reason about
worker scheduling — which is exactly the coupling the lease exists to avoid.

ProcessingRunSummary.title: ProcessingRunSummary
ProcessingRunSummary.description:
One attempt, as an operator sees it.

Absent on purpose:

  * `error_message` — server-authored today, but it is an unconstrained Text
    column with no CHECK and no test holding that line. One future
    `ProcessingFailed(stage, code, str(exc))` would put a parser library's
    exception text — which quotes document content and local paths — into a
    cross-user feed. `failed_stage` and `error_code` are a closed vocabulary
    and say the same thing about what went wrong.
  * the lease owner — a hostname and pid. Useful to an operator, but it
    names infrastructure, and `leased` plus `heartbeat_at` answers the
    actual question ("is anyone on this, and when were they last alive?").

ProcessingStageEvent.title: ProcessingStageEvent
ProcessingStageEvent.description:
One stage of one run.

`detail` is projected to `code` and `classification` only. The column is
unconstrained JSONB documented as "counts, codes and engine names only" —
true of every writer today, enforced by nothing.

ProfileVersionSummary.title: ProfileVersionSummary
ProfileVersionSummary.description: A version without its snapshot, for listings.

ProjectItemRead.title: ProjectItemRead
ProjectItemRead.description:
A project as returned. `technologies` and `links` are always present on
the way out.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: Text copied verbatim from that page. Never paraphrased.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Where a claim came from, and how sure the model was.

ResumeCandidate.title: ResumeCandidate
ResumeCandidate.description: The structured reading of one resume.

ResumeDocumentRead.title: ResumeDocumentRead
ResumeDocumentRead.description: An uploaded resume, with the state of its most recent attempt.

Snapshot.title: Snapshot
Snapshot.description: The complete confirmed-career-data document for one version.

SnapshotRead.title: SnapshotRead
SnapshotRead.description:
The snapshot as returned.

Separate from `Snapshot` because the two directions genuinely differ: on the
way in every collection is optional and defaults to empty, on the way out
every collection is always present. Collapsing them would force generated
clients to null-check five arrays that can never be null.

StructuredResultRead.title: StructuredResultRead
StructuredResultRead.description:
The AI reading, for the review screen.

Includes provenance, because the point of the review step is that a human
can check a claim against the page it came from.

TailoredContact.title: TailoredContact
TailoredContact.description:
Who this resume is from, and how to reply to it.

Every field is a column on the profile version, read off the user's own
resume and confirmed by them. None of it is composed, inferred or formatted:
`grounding._check_contact` compares each one to the stored column exactly,
so a "tidied" phone number or a name in a different case is an error rather
than a nicety.

Nullable throughout, because the profile's own columns are: a confirmed
version whose resume gave no phone number has no phone number, and printing
a blank line is better than any of the ways a generator might fill one in.

TailoredExperience.title: TailoredExperience
TailoredExperience.description:
One job, as it should appear on this resume.

The identity fields are copied, not generated: a company name or a job title
that has been "improved" is a lie with a straight face, and `grounding.py`
checks each of these against the snapshot row exactly.

TailoredLine.title: TailoredLine
TailoredLine.description:
One generated sentence, and the snapshot text behind it.

`text` is what appears in the document. `source_quote` is what the snapshot
actually said. They are usually close — the deterministic generator mostly
selects and re-punctuates — and the point of keeping both is that a reader
can see the distance between them rather than being asked to trust it.

TailoredLink.title: TailoredLink
TailoredLink.description: One link in the header. Both halves are transcribed from a link row.

TailoredResumeDocument.title: TailoredResumeDocument
TailoredResumeDocument.description:
One generated resume, aimed at one job.

`targeted_requirements` is the generator saying which of the posting's
requirements it tried to answer. It is not a claim about the candidate and
is not grounded against the snapshot — it is grounded against the JOB, and
the review screen shows it so the user can see what the document was
optimising for. An empty list is honest when the generator had nothing to
aim at.

is_approved.title: Is Approved
is_approved.description:
Whether this document may be downloaded.

Derived on the server so a client cannot invent its own rule. The same
predicate `service.get_artifact` applies before handing over bytes — a
UI that disagreed with it would show a download button that 409s.

TailoredResumeRead.title: TailoredResumeRead
TailoredResumeRead.description:
The generated document and the verdict on it.

The document is returned even when grounding failed. That is deliberate and
it is the honest choice: hiding a rejected document would leave the user
unable to see what was wrong with it, and the artifact — the thing that
could be sent to an employer — is withheld instead.

TailoredSkillGroup.title: TailoredSkillGroup
TailoredSkillGroup.description:
Skills, grouped for reading rather than re-stated.

Every name must appear in the snapshot's skills or in a project's
technologies. Grouping and ordering are the generator's contribution; the
set of skills is not.

TailoringIssueRead.title: TailoringIssueRead
TailoringIssueRead.description: One grounding finding, as the review screen shows it.

profile_version_id.title: Profile Version Id
profile_version_id.description: The confirmed profile version to tailor from. Defaults to the caller's current confirmed version. Drafts are refused.

match_result_id.title: Match Result Id
match_result_id.description: A match for this job, used to decide what to lead with. Never used to claim a requirement the profile does not evidence.

TailoringRequest.title: TailoringRequest
TailoringRequest.description: What a caller may ask for when starting a tailoring run.

is_terminal.title: Is Terminal
is_terminal.description: Whether this attempt has stopped. Everything else is in progress.

TailoringRunDetail.title: TailoringRunDetail
TailoringRunDetail.description: A run in full, with the document it produced and every finding on it.

is_terminal.title: Is Terminal
is_terminal.description: Whether this attempt has stopped. Everything else is in progress.

TailoringRunSummary.title: TailoringRunSummary
TailoringRunSummary.description: A tailoring run as it appears in a listing: state, not content.

UnmappedItem.title: UnmappedItem
UnmappedItem.description:
Something the resume contained that the profile snapshot cannot hold.

Recorded rather than silently dropped. An experience with no date is the
common case: `experiences.start_date` is NOT NULL in the profile schema, and
inventing a date to satisfy it would be exactly the fabrication this design
exists to prevent.
